$comment: Front matter is parsed twice: once in Rust, by `parse_front_matter` in
crates/essay-render/src/convert.rs, which decides what the document is
typeset as; and once in TypeScript, by `readFrontMatter` in
apps/desktop/src/lib/frontMatter.ts, which decides what the pickers show
and write. Two languages means two parsers — that part is not fixable.
What is fixable is the drift, and this is how: both sides read this file
and must produce the same answer for every case in it.
The failure this prevents is quiet. If the two disagree, the format menu
shows a tick beside a format the typesetter is not using, and the author
is looking at a page that says one thing and a control that says another.
Nothing throws. Nobody finds out until a document prints wrong.
The odd cases are here on purpose: they are the Rust parser's actual
behaviour, not an idealised YAML. Anything added here has to be checked
against what Rust really does, not against what it ought to do.
`expect` holds only the keys the renderer acts on. A key not listed is
